name: יַחְדּוֹ
summary: A man of Gad, son of Buz and father of Jeshishai, named once in the line of Abihail's sons who lived in Gilead and Bashan (1Ch 5:11, 14). The name is the root's יַחַד “union, together” with “his”, or the adverb itself (יַחְדּוֹ beside יַחְדָּו); scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “These were the sons of Abihail … son of Jeshishai, son of יַחְדּוֹ, son of Buz.”
“The sons of Gad dwelt over against them, in the land of Bashan.”
The noun יַחַד “union”: “my heart shall be toward you לְיָחַד”.
“For brothers to dwell גַּם־יָחַד, even as one.”

note: Takes j.be.ae (1 token). BDB's lemma is יַחְדֹּי (Baer's text); the corpus spells יַחְדּוֹ, the TIPNR form. Whether the name is the noun with the third person suffix (“his union”) or the adverb is not decided by the form; both are the root's sense.
